bug_semantics: The authenticated Administration Console endpoint /shared/instanceStatus.jsf copies the attacker-controlled GET parameter instanceName into pageSession.instanceName and then emits it without HTML-attribute encoding inside an f:verbatim fragment as <span class="instance-name" data-instancename="#{pageSession.instanceName}"/>. A remote attacker can send an authenticated console user a crafted URL whose quote-bearing instanceName value terminates data-instancename and adds an autofocus/onfocus handler; when the victim requests the fragment, attacker JavaScript executes in the victim's GlassFish console origin and session.
flaw_origin: Commit e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a introduced asynchronous instance-status refreshes and created instanceStatus.jsf. The new page reads request parameter instanceName at line 21 and reflects that value directly into an HTML attribute under f:verbatim at line 37. This raw request-to-attribute data flow, rather than the pre-existing status lookup, is the smallest causal origin of the reflected XSS.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names human author and committer Ondro Mihalyi <mihalyi@omnifish.ee>; its only trailer is exactly "Signed-off-by:Ondro Mihalyi <mihalyi@omnifish.ee>". It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party report https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/vulnerability-reports/-/issues/226 identifies GlassFish 7.0.15, victim authentication to the Administration Console, endpoint /shared/instanceStatus.jsf, GET parameter instanceName, and a quote/autofocus/onfocus payload for reflected JavaScript execution. The linked CNA item is https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/cve-assignement/-/issues/40; the published advisory is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vqrm-83g6-pfv4.

git show e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a shows a single-parent 2023-05-25 commit titled 'Admin Console: Update instance status asynchronously' that creates appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf. In that added file, line 21 executes getRequestValue(key="instanceName" value="#{pageSession.instanceName}"), while line 37 places #{pageSession.instanceName} directly in data-instancename inside f:verbatim. The same commit adds browser code that fetches /shared/instanceStatus.jsf?instanceName=... and assigns req.responseText to innerHTML.

git log main -L 21,37:appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf and git log --all -S searches for both 'data-instancename="#{pageSession.instanceName}"' and 'instanceStatus.jsf?instanceName=' resolve only to e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a, establishing the smallest line-writing BIC rather than a later move, release, revert, or refactor.

Direct parent-tree check 'git ls-tree -r 28b915e73f2839fd2f5d62ee22b4d204a1a432b8 -- appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf' returns no entry. The BIC creates the file from /dev/null, so the vulnerable request-to-verbatim-attribute path is absent from the immediate parent.

Version boundary: annotated tag 7.0.4 resolves to commit 0dd0bbdcf0d1c711e8c226a01a1b8ed7f951c06f and has no instanceStatus.jsf entry. Tag 7.0.5 resolves to 7b49f4eaf669e9a3b4f4648254f9016872455236 and contains blob f92b2ab6ffdff00a6eb43e39f6b4c2d09ec54ecd at that path. Thus this mechanism first ships in 7.0.5, before reported affected 7.0.15 (commit 6f2f4c26b0f825d36b45ef39f6f83ac6b56d438c), which contains the identical blob.

No fix exists in reachable history. The bundle advisory records vulnerable range <= 7.0.25 and first_patched_version null. Tags 7.0.25 (commit 17c9f164606e47efbc58907a97ad351a7f54089e) and even later 7.0.26 (commit 215b00392179abfef69725ff07455096f2e7fa19) both contain the exact original vulnerable blob f92b2ab6ffdff00a6eb43e39f6b4c2d09ec54ecd; current main 4a143866f4a92995e6387ee33f5412bdeac38567 does too. 'git log --all --follow' for the file has no commit after its introduction, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null and the advisory's <=7.0.25 upper bound is stale for this still-present mechanism.

BIC-only AI check: 'git cat-file commit e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a' shows tree 568adf242f859bfff441fc78d2ba31ed30a7709f, parent 28b915e73f2839fd2f5d62ee22b4d204a1a432b8, author and committer Ondro Mihalyi <mihalyi@omnifish.ee>, the two-line feature message, and only the human Signed-off-by trailer. No external PR, branch, later commit, or fix metadata was used for AI attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle starts when e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a changes status rendering from synchronous server-side table population to an AJAX HTML fragment. The fragment accepts instanceName directly from the request and writes it into a double-quoted data attribute in f:verbatim; the caller then inserts that response with innerHTML. This makes quote-bearing request data executable markup for an authenticated console victim. Line history and exact-string history both stop at this ordinary single-parent commit, and the immediate parent lacks the newly created endpoint, so no aggregate decomposition is needed and e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a is the smallest real BIC. The BIC falls between tags 7.0.4 and 7.0.5, is present unchanged in the reported 7.0.15 and advisory-bound 7.0.25, and remains byte-identical in 7.0.26 and current main; therefore the public lifecycle is still unpatched rather than having a discoverable fix commit. Finally, the BIC commit object contains only a human author/committer and human Signed-off-by trailer, with no AI marker. Under BIC-only attribution that proves NOT_AI independently of the missing remediation.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability remains unpatched in the reachable public history: there is no fix or direct-fix SHA, the advisory names no first patched version, and the original vulnerable blob persists through tag 7.0.26 and current main. This is a remediation/version-range gap, not an attribution gap; the advisory's published <=7.0.25 range should be updated for later releases while the sink remains unchanged.
